newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says fuel rebate changes fair.
newsitem.headline: Australia says fuel rebate changes fair.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday any changes in the government's diesel fuel rebate scheme for miners would be fair and reasonable.
Howard did not detail the planned changes, but there has been widespread speculation that total payouts would be capped in a continuing revamp aimed at reining in the cost.

"... The proposals put forward by the government will be seen by the mining industry as fair and reasonable and utterly consonant with our responsibility to the generality of the Australian community," Howard told Parliament.
The scheme provides a tax rebate to farmers and miners for diesel fuel for off-road use.
Payouts to miners blew out to an estimated A$823.4 million in 1996/97 from an original budget projection of A$749.8 million and is forecast at A$812.9 million in the fiscal year from July.
"The mining industry has been treated very fairly ineeded and it will continue to be treated very fairly," Howard said.
The government has not revealed how the cost will be contained, but Finance Minister John Fahey has said the government will consult the industry.
